content.content:
1	A cordless handheld vacuum lifter is used to move glass panes, stone slabs, and similar flat panels on site by suction gripping. A suction cup is pressed against the face of the panel, air is removed from the space enclosed between the cup and the panel, and the resulting difference between atmospheric pressure and the pressure in that enclosed space clamps the cup to the panel so that the panel can be carried.
2	
3	A suction grip is only as good as its seal. Dust on the panel, a textured or porous surface, a nick in the sealing lip, a change in temperature, or simply the slow permeation and leakage that occurs over minutes of handling will all bleed air back into the enclosed space. As air returns, the clamping force falls. The failure is progressive and, from the point of view of the person holding the panel, silent: nothing about the feel of the tool changes until the cup lets go, at which point a heavy panel is already falling.
4	
5	Vacuum lifting equipment has therefore long been fitted with vacuum monitoring. In one known lifter for transporting loads having an adhesion surface, a suction plate assembly carries projecting annular seals defining a vacuum chamber connected to a main vacuum source, a battery-fed emergency vacuum source that can be started by an emergency switch is additionally provided, and a pressure pickup associated with the vacuum chamber is coupled with a malfunction alarm such that the alarm is turned on when a preset limit pressure is exceeded during vacuum operation [REF:US-5310232-A]. That equipment is a suction plate assembly with a main vacuum source and a separate emergency vacuum source; the alarm is described as a malfunction alarm tied to a preset limit pressure, and the reference does not describe the limit pressure in terms of the vacuum still needed to keep hold of the load.
6	
7	Control systems for vacuum lift equipment have also been described in which a programmable controller interprets feedback from vacuum level sensors and battery sensors and responsively provides warnings and limits or alters machine functions, including evaluating a change in measured vacuum level over time to determine a rate of vacuum level change that may be caused by a leak and outputting a warning indication when that rate exceeds a threshold rate [REF:US-10518985-B2]. Such a system is built around a controller with memory, stored records, and machine-function interlocks, and its leak warning is a response to how fast the vacuum is changing rather than to where the vacuum sits relative to the point at which the grip would fail.
8	
9	Powered suction devices in a hand-carried format are also known. An electric vacuum suction lifter has been described having a main body with a suction surface carrying first and second annular sealing units that bound a sealed space, a control unit, a vacuum pump controlled by the control unit to draw air from the sealed space, a pressure sensing unit that measures the pressure of the sealed space to generate instant pressure information, a battery unit that is charged by external power equipment and powers the control unit, pump, and pressure sensing unit, a start button, a pressure relief button, and at least one handle by which a member gripped by the device can be carried [REF:US-10625955-B2]. In that device the instant pressure information is compared with a high predetermined pressure and a low predetermined pressure: reaching the high predetermined pressure stops the pump, and falling below the low predetermined pressure restarts the pump. A warning unit is described as being operated when the detected battery power is below a predetermined battery power, and warning information relating to pressure is described as being transmitted to an external electronic device. A closely similar electric suction cup has likewise been described, in which the pressure detection unit detects the pressure between the suction cup and the component in real time and the vacuum pump automatically acts again when that pressure is lower than a second predetermined pressure [REF:CN-110630621-B].
10	
11	Other hand-carried powered suction devices have likewise been described. A cordless wand device for grasping objects such as silicon wafers has a housing with a hollow interior, a tip attached to the housing through a hollow tube and having a perimeter region contoured to form an airtight seal when placed against the surface of the object, a power source and a vacuum pump positioned within the housing, a switch by which the pump is turned on and off, and light-emitting diodes of different colours which indicate to an operator whether the power source is sufficiently charged to generate sufficient suction force to safely grasp the object, the sufficiency being determined from the voltage drop across a resistor network fed by the power source [REF:US-5374090-A]. What is indicated there is the state of the power source and the sufficiency of the suction force for taking hold, not how much hold remains on an object already being carried.
12	
13	A portable electric carrying suction cup structure has been described in which a handle is fixed to the upper end of a suction cup body and a vacuum pump is provided on the suction cup body, with a control unit connected between the pump and the power supply part, so that air is pumped out from between the suction cup body and the surface of a smooth material and is continuously pumped out after an airtight state has been reached in order to avoid loosening and falling during movement; the control unit is provided with a pressure gauge by which the user can know the pressure change, with a light source displaying different usage states, and with a buzzer for sending out alarm sounds according to different usage states [REF:CN-2806399-Y]. Here again the answer to a decaying grip is to keep the pump running, and what the buzzer is tied to is a usage state rather than the amount of grip left.
14	
15	A digital display suction cup has been described comprising a suction cup and a handle structure, the two ends of the handle structure carrying a switch button and a pressure relief valve, the handle structure carrying a battery and an electric vacuum pump connected to the suction cup through an air pipe, and the lower part of the battery end carrying an air pressure sensor and a display screen which displays the negative pressure value of the suction cup and the battery power, the battery being charged through a USB charging port [REF:US-2024424646-A1]. That device puts a number in front of the user and leaves the reading of the number, and the judgement of what it means for the panel in hand, to the user.
16	
17	A portable hand grab has been described including one or more suction cups, at least one handle connected to the suction cups, at least one electrical vacuum pump for at least partially evacuating a suction volume between the suction cups and the attachment surfaces, at least one vacuum sensor for detecting a vacuum level in the suction volume, a power storage unit, and an electronic controller configured to control the pump to evacuate the suction volume when the vacuum sensor detects the vacuum level being less than a preselected minimum vacuum level, together with an attach indicator which the controller activates when the vacuum sensor detects the vacuum level being greater than a preselected safe vacuum level [REF:WO-2017156581-A1]. The indicator there reports that attachment has been achieved, being activated above a preselected safe vacuum level, and the response to a vacuum level below the preselected minimum is once more to run the pump.
18	
19	A sucker for plate glass has also been described in which the sucker body defines a suction hole at its suction surface and carries a manually operated vacuum pump, a sensor communicating with the suction channel that connects the two suction holes and including a piston lever which moves in proportion to the degree of vacuum, a switch closed by the piston lever when the degree of vacuum reaches a predetermined value, a power source, and a sound generator which generates sound when the switch is closed [REF:US-5184858-A]. The pump in that sucker is worked by hand, and the sound is generated when the sensor detects a predetermined degree of vacuum, the passages of record describing that value only as a predetermined value.
20	
21	Multi-cup handling equipment has been described in which two or more vacuum modules are mounted on a mounting frame, each module having a cup, an electrically powered vacuum pump, a fluid circuit, a controller, and optionally a pressure sensor and a battery, with an interface through which a user selects an operational mode of the modules, and in which each module may include indicators that indicate a functional condition of the module visually or audibly [REF:WO-2022236379-A1].
22	
23	Two shortcomings persist for a person who is holding a panel in one hand. First, the response to a decaying grip in the known powered devices is to run the pump again: the device treats a falling vacuum as a housekeeping event to be corrected, and neither [REF:US-10625955-B2] nor [REF:CN-110630621-B] relates the low predetermined pressure at which it acts to the vacuum still needed to hold the load. If the leak is larger than the pump can make up - a torn lip, a dusty or porous panel, a cracked substrate - the pump simply runs while the grip continues to decay, and any signal that is given is tied to the low predetermined pressure at which the pump is restarted, or is transmitted to an external electronic device, rather than to the vacuum still needed to hold the load. Second, where a signal is given at all, it is given on a condition unrelated to the hold on the load (battery state or charge sufficiency), on a rate of change, on a usage state, on the achievement of attachment above a safe level, or at a preset or predetermined value whose relationship to the load-holding capacity of the cup is not established. None of these guarantees the one thing a person carrying a slab actually needs: notice that arrives while the cup is still holding, with grip left over to get the panel down.
24	
25	There remains a need for a self-contained, cordless, hand-held vacuum lifter that tells the user that the grip is failing at a point on the decay curve at which the grip has not yet failed.
26

A cordless wand device for grasping objects such as silicon wafers has a housing with a hollow interior, a tip attached to the housing through a hollow tube and having a perimeter region contoured to form an airtight seal when placed against the surface of the object, a power source and a vacuum pump positioned within the housing, a switch by which the pump is turned on and off, and light-emitting diodes of different colours which indicate to an operator whether the power source is sufficiently charged to generate sufficient suction force to safely grasp the object, the sufficiency being determined from the voltage drop across a resistor network fed by the power source [REF:US-5374090-A]. What is indicated there is the state of the power source and the sufficiency of the suction force for taking hold, not how much hold remains on an object already being carried.

A portable electric carrying suction cup structure has been described in which a handle is fixed to the upper end of a suction cup body and a vacuum pump is provided on the suction cup body, with a control unit connected between the pump and the power supply part, so that air is pumped out from between the suction cup body and the surface of a smooth material and is continuously pumped out after an airtight state has been reached in order to avoid loosening and falling during movement; the control unit is provided with a pressure gauge by which the user can know the pressure change, with a light source displaying different usage states, and with a buzzer for sending out alarm sounds according to different usage states [REF:CN-2806399-Y]. Here again the answer to a decaying grip is to keep the pump running, and what the buzzer is tied to is a usage state rather than the amount of grip left.

A digital display suction cup has been described comprising a suction cup and a handle structure, the two ends of the handle structure carrying a switch button and a pressure relief valve, the handle structure carrying a battery and an electric vacuum pump connected to the suction cup through an air pipe, and the lower part of the battery end carrying an air pressure sensor and a display screen which displays the negative pressure value of the suction cup and the battery power, the battery being charged through a USB charging port [REF:US-2024424646-A1]. That device puts a number in front of the user and leaves the reading of the number, and the judgement of what it means for the panel in hand, to the user.

A portable hand grab has been described including one or more suction cups, at least one handle connected to the suction cups, at least one electrical vacuum pump for at least partially evacuating a suction volume between the suction cups and the attachment surfaces, at least one vacuum sensor for detecting a vacuum level in the suction volume, a power storage unit, and an electronic controller configured to control the pump to evacuate the suction volume when the vacuum sensor detects the vacuum level being less than a preselected minimum vacuum level, together with an attach indicator which the controller activates when the vacuum sensor detects the vacuum level being greater than a preselected safe vacuum level [REF:WO-2017156581-A1]. The indicator there reports that attachment has been achieved, being activated above a preselected safe vacuum level, and the response to a vacuum level below the preselected minimum is once more to run the pump.

A sucker for plate glass has also been described in which the sucker body defines a suction hole at its suction surface and carries a manually operated vacuum pump, a sensor communicating with the suction channel that connects the two suction holes and including a piston lever which moves in proportion to the degree of vacuum, a switch closed by the piston lever when the degree of vacuum reaches a predetermined value, a power source, and a sound generator which generates sound when the switch is closed [REF:US-5184858-A]. The pump in that sucker is worked by hand, and the sound is generated when the sensor detects a predetermined degree of vacuum, the passages of record describing that value only as a predetermined value.

Multi-cup handling equipment has been described in which two or more vacuum modules are mounted on a mounting frame, each module having a cup, an electrically powered vacuum pump, a fluid circuit, a controller, and optionally a pressure sensor and a battery, with an interface through which a user selects an operational mode of the modules, and in which each module may include indicators that indicate a functional condition of the module visually or audibly [REF:WO-2022236379-A1].

Two shortcomings persist for a person who is holding a panel in one hand. First, the response to a decaying grip in the known powered devices is to run the pump again: the device treats a falling vacuum as a housekeeping event to be corrected, and neither [REF:US-10625955-B2] nor [REF:CN-110630621-B] relates the low predetermined pressure at which it acts to the vacuum still needed to hold the load. If the leak is larger than the pump can make up - a torn lip, a dusty or porous panel, a cracked substrate - the pump simply runs while the grip continues to decay, and any signal that is given is tied to the low predetermined pressure at which the pump is restarted, or is transmitted to an external electronic device, rather than to the vacuum still needed to hold the load. Second, where a signal is given at all, it is given on a condition unrelated to the hold on the load (battery state or charge sufficiency), on a rate of change, on a usage state, on the achievement of attachment above a safe level, or at a preset or predetermined value whose relationship to the load-holding capacity of the cup is not established. None of these guarantees the one thing a person carrying a slab actually needs: notice that arrives while the cup is still holding, with grip left over to get the panel down.

There remains a need for a self-contained, cordless, hand-held vacuum lifter that tells the user that the grip is failing at a point on the decay curve at which the grip has not yet failed.

input.summary:
Ledger scope: 16 reference numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 22, 30, 32, 40, 50, 100, 202-210), 6 claims (3 apparatus, 3 method), four figure briefs, and all ten draft sections were traced against input/disclosure.md and the USER passages of input/conversation.md.

Supported and clean. Every claim limitation traces to an exact affirmative passage: "a rigid body comprising a handle"; "a suction cup carried by the rigid body, the suction cup comprising a flexible sealing lip"; "an electric vacuum pump disposed within the rigid body ... configured to draw air through a port to create a vacuum"; "a pressure sensor configured to monitor the vacuum"; "a warning indicator driven by the pressure sensor ... configured to activate when the vacuum is lost"; "a rechargeable battery configured to power the electric vacuum pump"; claim 2/5 ("warn a user before a load can be dropped"); claim 3/6 ("for glass and stone panels"). The numeral assignments 10/12/14/16/20/22/30/32/40 are the inventor's own; 50, 100 and the 202-210 step numerals are drafting assignments over disclosed subject matter. Formalities match input/brief.md: title, "Not applicable." in cross-reference and government support. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative remains anywhere in draft/ or figures/ (the "QA MARKER ONE" text referenced in the conversation is gone). The prior three-level warning/release-threshold scheme, the 20-claim ladder, and the FIG. 4 vacuum-level plot described in the drafting agent's own YOU message are absent from the current text, as they must be — that message is not inventor support. Section-line designation is consistent across all three places: FIG. 1 brief ("The repeated designation 2 is placed at both endpoints, so this is line 2-2"), draft/07-drawings.md ("taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 1"), and the FIG. 2 brief ("taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 1"). Numeral coverage per sheet matches the briefs and numerals.md exactly, each numeral means one thing, and claims, summary, description and abstract use the same relationships and terms throughout. Background prior-art characterizations are outside my remit and were not assessed.

Five untraced items found, all additions of technical substance the inventor never wrote:

1. draft/08 asserts an atmospheric-pressure clamping load path through the body and handle to the workpiece. The disclosure says only that the pump creates a vacuum and that the sensor "monitors the grip vacuum".
2. draft/08 asserts an operating relationship — that running the pump "increases the vacuum" and that "air leaking back is a loss of vacuum and a weakening of the grip". This reads as residue of the withdrawn positive-magnitude vacuum convention; nothing in the disclosure describes pump-driven vacuum increase or leak-back behaviour.
3. draft/08 asserts the cause of vacuum loss (imperfect lip seal → air bleeds back → progressive loss). The disclosure states only that the indicator "activates when vacuum is lost".
4. The FIG. 2 brief asserts handle topology and position: the handle is cut once by the plane and sits "above the upper wall of the shell". Count/topology and relative location are substantive even under a schematic convention, and no source passage places or shapes the handle — the disclosure says only "The rigid body 14 also includes a handle 16." The generic grip outline in FIG. 1 remains an acceptable depiction convention; the cut-region count and location do not.
5. The FIG. 1 brief asserts a relative proportion — the slab "extending past both sides of the lifter". Break lines already carry indeterminate extent; the added phrase is a size relationship with no source.

Each fix is a deletion or a narrowing back to disclosed substance; none requires adding a speculative shape or optional embodiment. No claim, numeral, terminology, or figure-to-text inconsistency was found beyond items 4 and 5, and no formalities defect was found.

findings.title: Detailed description asserts an undisclosed operating relationship: running the pump increases the vacuum, and leak-back weakens the grip
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The electric vacuum pump 20 is disposed within the rigid body 14" (final sentence)
findings.detail: The sentence states a quantitative operating behaviour of the device — that continued pump operation raises the vacuum, and that returning air lowers it and weakens the grip. This is a vacuum-polarity/behaviour convention, not a restatement of anything the inventor wrote, and it is the residue of the withdrawn scheme in which grip vacuum was defined as a positive magnitude so that "greater than" and "falls to" had a fixed sense. No affirmative USER passage describes pump operation increasing vacuum, air leaking back, or grip weakening as a function of vacuum. The drafting agent's own YOU message describing that convention is not inventor support.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Running the electric vacuum pump 20 draws further air through the port 22 and increases the vacuum; air leaking back is a loss of vacuum and a weakening of the grip." Nearest source (input/disclosure.md): "An electric vacuum pump 20 is disposed inside the rigid body 14 and is configured to draw air through a port 22 to create a vacuum. A pressure sensor 30 monitors the grip vacuum." and "The pressure sensor 30 drives a warning indicator 32, which activates when vacuum is lost." There is no affirmative passage on increasing vacuum, leak-back, or grip weakening.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence "Running the electric vacuum pump 20 draws further air through the port 22 and increases the vacuum; air leaking back is a loss of vacuum and a weakening of the grip." in full. The preceding sentences already state the supported substance (the pump draws air through the port 22 to create the vacuum, and a load is retained on the suction cup 10 by the vacuum).

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief asserts undisclosed handle topology and relative location (single cut region above the upper wall)
findings.detail: The brief fixes how many times the cutting plane meets the handle (once) and where the handle sits relative to the body shell (above its upper wall). A cut-region count is a topology assertion — it tells the reader the handle is solid across the centre plane rather than a loop or two-limb arch — and "above the upper wall of the shell" is a relative location. Both convey technical substance and so must trace even though the parts are drawn schematically. The disclosure assigns the handle no shape, no topology and no position; the only source sentence is a bare inclusion statement. The drafting agent's YOU message reciting the arch and the single cut region, and its statement that this was made "as the review directed", are context and never inventor support. FIG. 1's "plain generic grip outline" may remain as a depiction convention; the count and the position may not.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Where the cutting plane meets the handle, the handle is shown as a single cut region above the upper wall of the shell, cross-hatched and unnumbered." Nearest source (input/disclosure.md): "The rigid body 14 also includes a handle 16." There is no affirmative passage describing the handle's shape, its cross-sectional topology, or its position relative to the rigid body.
findings.fix: Replace that bullet with: "Where the cutting plane meets the handle, the handle is shown cut, cross-hatched and unnumbered, in agreement with the generic grip outline of FIG. 1." Make no change to draft/07-drawings.md, draft/08-detailed-description.md, numerals.md, or any other brief; numeral coverage for FIG. 2 (10, 12, 14, 20, 22, 50) is unaffected because the cut region is unnumbered.

findings.title: Detailed description asserts an undisclosed atmospheric-clamping load path through the rigid body and handle
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The electric vacuum pump 20 is disposed within the rigid body 14" (second sentence)
findings.detail: The sentence explains the gripping mechanism (surrounding atmospheric pressure acting on the outside of the cup) and states a load path in which the cup, and with it the rigid body 14 and the handle 16, are clamped to the workpiece 50. The mechanism and the clamped-together relationship of cup, body and handle are engineering explanation supplied by the drafter, not inventor text. Only the end result — that a load is retained on the suction cup by the vacuum — traces to the disclosure, via "grip vacuum" and "before a load can be dropped".
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The pressure of the surrounding atmosphere acting on the outside of the suction cup 10 then clamps the suction cup 10, and with it the rigid body 14 and the handle 16, to the workpiece 50, so that a load is retained on the suction cup 10 by the vacuum." Nearest source (input/disclosure.md): "A pressure sensor 30 monitors the grip vacuum." and "The warning indicator 32 is configured to warn a user before a load can be dropped." No affirmative passage mentions atmospheric pressure, clamping, or a load path through the body and handle.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "A load is retained on the suction cup 10 by the vacuum." This keeps the wording used in claim 1, claim 4, the summary and the abstract, so no other section needs editing.

findings.title: Detailed description asserts an undisclosed cause and progression of vacuum loss
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The warning function operates as follows" (final sentence)
findings.detail: The sentence supplies a failure mechanism for the claimed device: an imperfect seal between the flexible sealing lip 12 and the workpiece 50, air bleeding back, and progressive loss of vacuum. The disclosure states the triggering condition only as "when vacuum is lost" and says nothing about seal imperfection, bleed-back, or a progressive decay. This is drafter-supplied engineering explanation, and it also carries over the decay framing of the withdrawn threshold scheme.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "If the seal between the flexible sealing lip 12 and the workpiece 50 is imperfect, air bleeds back and the vacuum is progressively lost." Nearest source (input/disclosure.md): "The pressure sensor 30 drives a warning indicator 32, which activates when vacuum is lost." No affirmative passage identifies why or how the vacuum is lost.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence "If the seal between the flexible sealing lip 12 and the workpiece 50 is imperfect, air bleeds back and the vacuum is progressively lost." in full. The paragraph then reads: "The warning function operates as follows. The electric vacuum pump 20 creates the vacuum, the user lifts and carries the workpiece 50, and the load is retained on the suction cup 10 by the vacuum." and is followed by the supported activation paragraph, so nothing else changes.

findings.title: FIG. 1 brief asserts an undisclosed relative proportion between the workpiece and the lifter
findings.detail: "Extending past both sides of the lifter" is a relative-size and relative-location statement about the panel and the tool, which is substantive rather than a page-placement convention. The break lines already discharge the drawing's need to show indeterminate extent without asserting a size; the added phrase goes further and fixes the panel as larger than the lifter on both sides. The disclosure identifies the workpiece only by material and format and says nothing about its size relative to the lifter.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The workpiece 50 is a flat slab, broken off at each end with break lines to show indeterminate extent, extending past both sides of the lifter." Nearest source (input/disclosure.md): "A cordless handheld vacuum lifter for glass and stone panels is disclosed." No affirmative passage gives the panel's dimensions or its extent relative to the lifter.
findings.fix: Replace that bullet with: "The workpiece 50 is a flat slab, broken off at each end with break lines to show indeterminate extent." Leave the numeral anchor for 50 ("well inside the slab, to the right of the suction cup") and the numeral coverage for FIG. 1 (10, 12, 14, 16, 50, 100) unchanged.
